verdicts.reading: Manufactured or lab-grown blood substitutes start to be used for transfusion in health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of transfusions use a substitute by 2022 = hit; real use below 5% (pilots, niche approvals) or 5% in 2023-2025 = partial; no real use by 2025 = miss.
verdicts.reason: No substitute is approved in the US or EU; Hemopure is approved only in South Africa and Russia and sees niche use. The first lab-grown red cells were transfused to volunteers in the RESTORE trial in Nov 2022. Real use exists only as niche approvals and a first-in-human pilot, far below 5% of transfusions.

evidence.title: First ever clinical trial of laboratory grown red blood cells being transfused into another person
evidence.shows: RESTORE trial: first two people transfused with lab-grown red cells; research stage.

evidence.title: Blood substitute (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Fluosol was the only FDA-approved oxygen therapeutic (1989, withdrawn 1994); Hemopure approved only in South Africa and Russia; none approved in the US.

verdicts.reading: Therapies that regrow or repair damaged human tissue start to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of relevant procedures (e.g. cartilage repair, chronic wound care) use regenerative tissue products by 2022 = hit; real but smaller use = partial; none by 2025 = miss.
verdicts.reason: Approved regenerative products are in routine use: MACI autologous chondrocyte implants (FDA, re-approved through 2024) and cellular skin substitutes for chronic wounds. No source found showing they reach 5% of the relevant procedures by 2022; use is real but niche.

evidence.title: MACI (Autologous Cultured Chondrocytes on a Porcine Collagen Membrane)
evidence.shows: FDA-approved cultured-cell scaffold that repairs knee cartilage defects; in clinical use.

evidence.title: Approved Cellular and Gene Therapy Products
evidence.shows: Small list of approved cell-based regenerative products, indicating niche, specialised use.

verdicts.reading: Engineered or bioartificial blood vessels for implantation start to be used in health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of vascular grafting procedures use engineered vessels by 2022 = hit; real use below 5% or 5% in 2023-2025 = partial; no real use by 2025 = miss.
verdicts.reason: The first tissue-engineered vessel (Humacyte Symvess) was FDA-approved in Dec 2024 for extremity vascular trauma, inside the 5-year window. Use in 2025 is niche (one indication, early launch). Conventional synthetic Dacron/ePTFE grafts predate the poster and are not what the label means.

evidence.title: FDA Approves First Acellular Tissue Engineered Vessel to Treat Vascular Trauma in Extremities
evidence.shows: First approval of a tissue-engineered vessel, late 2024; no earlier routine use.

verdicts.reading: Pharmaceuticals made by 3D printing, including patient-tailored dosing, start to be dispensed in health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of dispensed drugs or pharmacies by 2022 = hit; real but niche use = partial; none by 2025 = miss.
verdicts.reason: Spritam (levetiracetam), the first 3D-printed drug, was FDA-approved in 2015 and marketed; hospital pilots of printed personalised doses followed. Use is real but a tiny share of prescriptions.

evidence.title: Spritam (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: First 3D-printed drug approved by FDA in 2015; no other approved printed drugs listed.

verdicts.reading: Stem-cell therapies for disease or injury (regenerative uses beyond the long-established bone-marrow transplant) start to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of patients in the target indications receive stem-cell therapy by 2022 = hit; real but niche approved use = partial; none by 2025 = miss.
verdicts.reason: Approved regenerative stem-cell products exist (EU Holoclar, Alofisel; US Ryoncil approved Dec 2024, Omisirge, Lantidra) and are used, but in narrow indications and small numbers. Haematopoietic stem-cell transplant was routine long before 2012 and is not the poster's forward-looking reading; under that reading the claim would be an earlier hit, noted as a minority reading.

evidence.title: Approved Cellular and Gene Therapy Products
evidence.shows: Approved stem-cell products are cord-blood HPC units plus a few MSC/islet products (Ryoncil, Omisirge, Lantidra), all narrow indications.

verdicts.reading: Genetic modification of embryos or fetuses before birth starts to be used in health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of relevant IVF/prenatal cases by 2022 = hit; real clinical use below 5% (licensed niche service) = partial; no real use by 2025 or abandoned = miss.
verdicts.reason: CRISPR embryo editing produced three babies in China (2018) and was criminalised, so that path is abandoned. But licensed mitochondrial donation (pronuclear transfer, a germline modification of the embryo) runs as an NHS clinical service in Newcastle (licensed 2017), with eight babies reported in July 2025. Real, licensed, tiny-scale use inside the window = partial. A strict 'nuclear gene editing' reading would give miss.

evidence.title: Eight babies born after Mitochondrial donation
evidence.shows: Licensed clinical mitochondrial donation by pronuclear transfer at Newcastle; eight babies born; licence granted 2017.

evidence.title: He Jiankui affair (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Only three CRISPR-edited babies (2018-2019); researcher jailed; China criminalised human germline editing in 2020.

verdicts.reading: Treatment selected or designed for a patient's genetics and other characteristics starts to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of relevant treatments or new therapies are biomarker-guided by 2022 = hit.
verdicts.reason: Personalized medicines made up 34% of FDA new molecular entity approvals in 2022 and at least 25% for eight years running; biomarker-guided oncology treatment and companion diagnostics are routine. Well above 5% by 2022.

evidence.title: Personalized Medicines Topped 25 Percent of New Drug Approvals for Eighth Year in a Row in 2022
evidence.shows: 12 personalized medicines, 34% of 2022 NMEs; >=25% each year 2015-2022.

verdicts.reading: Surgery performed with robotic systems starts to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of relevant surgical procedures are robot-assisted by 2022 = hit.
verdicts.reason: In 73 Michigan hospitals the robotic share of general surgery rose from 1.8% (2012) to 15.1% (2018), above 5% before the placed year. The remote (telesurgery) sense is not required by the label.

evidence.title: Trends in the Adoption of Robotic Surgery for Common Surgical Procedures (JAMA Netw Open)
evidence.shows: Robotic share of general surgery 1.8% in 2012 to 15.1% in 2018 (169,404 patients, 73 hospitals).

verdicts.reading: Diagnosis delivered through smartphone apps (mHealth) starts to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of relevant users (adults seeking diagnosis) used app-based diagnostics by 2022 = hit.
verdicts.reason: A July 2022 representative-style German survey found 6.5% of adults had used symptom checkers; FDA-cleared app diagnostics (Apple Watch ECG AF detection, 2018; KardiaMobile) were in wide consumer use. Just above the 5% line by 2022; margin is thin.

evidence.title: Characteristics of Users and Nonusers of Symptom Checkers in Germany: Cross-Sectional Survey Study
evidence.shows: Survey of 1,084 German residents, July 2022: 6.5% had used symptom checkers.

evidence.title: About one-in-five Americans use a smart watch or fitness tracker (Pew)
evidence.shows: 21% of US adults use a smartwatch or fitness tracker, the platform for app-based ECG/AF checks.

verdicts.reading: Software that understands patient and clinician language starts to be used in health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of clinicians or hospitals use clinical NLP/speech understanding by 2022 = hit.
verdicts.reason: Nuance Dragon Medical clinical speech recognition was used by over 550,000 physicians and Nuance solutions by 77% of US hospitals (July 2022). Clinical NLP for documentation and coding was routine before 2022.

evidence.title: Nuance Expands Dragon Medical One Availability through the Microsoft Marketplace
evidence.shows: Over 550,000 physicians use Dragon Medical; 77% of US hospitals use Nuance solutions.

verdicts.reading: Augmented-reality overlays guiding surgeons during operations start to be used in health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of relevant (e.g. spine, navigated) procedures use AR guidance by 2022 = hit; real use below 5% = partial; none by 2025 = miss.
verdicts.reason: Augmedics xvision was FDA-cleared Dec 2019, first US case June 2020, and reached 10,000 cumulative procedures only in April 2025; other AR systems are similarly small. Real routine use in some hospitals, far below 5% of spine surgeries (well over a million a year in the US).

evidence.title: First Augmented Reality Spine Surgery Using FDA-Cleared Augmedics xvision Spine System Completed in U.S.
evidence.shows: First US AR spine surgery at Johns Hopkins after Dec 2019 FDA clearance.

evidence.title: Augmedics Completes 10,000th Augmented Reality Spine Surgery With xvision Spine System
evidence.shows: Only 10,000 cumulative AR spine procedures by 2025: niche use.

verdicts.reading: Remote, software- or video-based assessment of care urgency starts to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of urgent-care contacts in a health system are triaged remotely by software by 2022 = hit.
verdicts.reason: England's NHS 111 triages about 16-20 million calls a year with the NHS Pathways clinical decision-support software (a registered medical device), a large share of urgent-care contacts for a population of ~56 million; COVID-era online and video triage expanded this. Above 5% by 2022 (and already before).

evidence.title: NHS Pathways is a Class 1 medical device (NHS England Digital)
evidence.shows: NHS Pathways is the software used to triage NHS 111 and 999 calls.

evidence.title: An analysis of NHS 111 demand for primary care services
evidence.shows: NHS 111 triages over 16.6 million calls per year with NHS Pathways.

verdicts.reading: Remote transmission of patient vital signs and device data to clinicians starts to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of relevant patients (e.g. implanted cardiac device holders, chronic-condition patients) are remotely monitored by 2022 = hit.
verdicts.reason: In 211,346 Medicare beneficiaries with new cardiac implantable devices (2015-2020), roughly two-thirds had at least one remote-monitoring encounter (over one-third had none); CMS added RPM billing codes in 2019. Well above 5% by 2022, though adherence to recommended frequency was low.

evidence.title: Cardiac implantable electronic device patient follow-up: Assessment of U.S. practice (Heart Rhythm)
evidence.shows: Medicare CIED cohort 2015-2020: over one-third never had remote monitoring, so most did; <5% at recommended frequency.

verdicts.reading: Blood-glucose monitoring without skin pricking or an implanted/inserted sensor starts to be used in health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of glucose-monitoring diabetics use it by 2022 = hit; real use below 5% = partial; no real use by 2025 = miss.
verdicts.reason: No non-invasive glucose monitor is FDA-authorised; in Feb 2024 FDA warned against smartwatches and rings claiming it. Diabetes care moved to minimally invasive CGMs (filament under the skin), which do not meet the label. A few CE-marked devices (e.g. GlucoTrack) never reached routine use, and GlucoTrack pivoted to an implantable sensor.

evidence.title: Do Not Use Smartwatches or Smart Rings to Measure Blood Glucose Levels: FDA Safety Communication
evidence.shows: FDA has not authorised any smartwatch or smart ring that measures blood glucose on its own.

verdicts.reading: Patient health records that are open, portable and accessible to patients and providers start to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of patients access their records online / via apps by 2022 = hit.
verdicts.reason: About 3 in 5 US individuals were offered and accessed their online medical record or patient portal in 2022 (ONC), backed by the 21st Century Cures Act information-blocking rule (2021) and FHIR app access. Far above 5%.

evidence.title: Individuals' Access and Use of Patient Portals and Smartphone Health Apps, 2022 (ONC Data Brief 69)
evidence.shows: ~57% of US individuals offered and accessed their online record in 2022, up 50% since 2020.

verdicts.reading: Thin skin-mounted electronic sensors ('electronic skin' patches) that monitor body signals start to be used in health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of relevant monitored patients (e.g. NICU, inpatients) use epidermal sensors by 2022 = hit; real clinical use below 5% = partial; none by 2025 = miss.
verdicts.reason: The Rogers-lab line reached clinic: Sibel Health's ANNE skin sensors gained FDA 510(k) clearances (ANNE One, May 2023, for neonates to adults; ANNE Maternal) and are deployed in some hospitals and low-income-country NICUs. Use is real but limited to pilots and early deployments, well under 5% of monitored patients. Conventional adhesive ECG patches are not the thin epidermal electronics the label names.

evidence.title: ANNE One wireless monitoring platform receives FDA clearance (AASM)
evidence.shows: FDA 510(k) for Sibel's ANNE One skin-mounted wireless sensors, neonates to adults.

evidence.title: Evaluation of Sibel's Advanced Neonatal Epidermal (ANNE) wireless continuous physiological monitor in Nairobi, Kenya
evidence.shows: Epidermal sensors at evaluation/pilot stage in neonatal care.

verdicts.reading: Computing systems like IBM Watson that answer clinical questions from large medical corpora start to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of clinicians use such systems by 2022 = hit; real use below 5% by 2022, or 5% reached 2023-2025 = partial; no real use by 2025 = miss.
verdicts.reason: Watson for Oncology had niche hospital deployments and was wound down when IBM sold Watson Health in 2022, so by 2022 use was well under 5%. LLM-based clinical QA then crossed the line: OpenEvidence was used by about 40% of US physicians by mid-2025 (60% claimed by Sept 2025). 5% reached within 3-5 years after 2020 = partial.

evidence.title: OpenEvidence, the Fastest-Growing Application for Physicians in History, Announces $210 Million Round
evidence.shows: OpenEvidence used by ~40% of US physicians by mid-2025 (company figure).

evidence.title: OpenEvidence (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Clinical question-answering system over medical literature; launched 2023.

verdicts.reading: Swallowable sensor pills that report from inside the body start to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of relevant diagnostic procedures or medication-adherence patients use ingestible sensors by 2022 = hit; real but niche use = partial; none or abandoned by 2025 = miss.
verdicts.reason: Sensor-in-pill adherence (Proteus, Abilify MyCite) reached market but was abandoned (Proteus bankrupt 2020; MyCite discontinued Oct 2024). Capsule endoscopy and motility capsules remain routine niche procedures (over 4 million PillCams sold) but are a small share of GI diagnostics and predate the poster. Real, niche use = partial; reading only the adherence-sensor line would give miss.

evidence.title: Abilify MyCite FDA Approval History (Drugs.com)
evidence.shows: Approved 2017; Otsuka discontinued US commercialisation in Oct 2024.

evidence.title: PillCam Capsule Endoscopy Platform (Medtronic brochure)
evidence.shows: More than 4 million PillCam capsules sold worldwide; ambulatory GI procedure.

verdicts.reading: Fast, cheap sequencing of a patient's genome or tumour for diagnosis starts to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of relevant patients (e.g. advanced cancer, rare disease, prenatal screening) receive sequencing-based diagnosis by 2022 = hit.
verdicts.reason: In a US cohort of 63,294 patients, NGS after metastatic diagnosis in 2021 reached 34.5% (breast) to 62.9% (colorectal) and 61.4% in advanced NSCLC; NGS-based prenatal cfDNA screening and rapid NICU genome sequencing are also routine. Far above 5% by 2022.

evidence.title: Next-Generation Sequencing Trends among Adult Patients with Select Advanced Tumor Types: A Real-World Evidence Evaluation (J Mol Diagn)
evidence.shows: 2021: NGS received by 34.5-62.9% of US patients with select metastatic tumours.

verdicts.reading: Diagnostic sensors used at home (external sensors) start to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of relevant patients use home diagnostic sensors by 2022 = hit (earlier counts).
verdicts.reason: Self-measured home blood-pressure monitoring was used by about 61% of US adults with hypertension in 2019 (20 states) and by ~37-39% monthly in NHANES 2009-2014; home glucose meters, pulse oximeters and home sleep tests are routine. Above 5% before the placed year.

evidence.title: Self-Measured Blood Pressure Monitoring Among Adults With Self-Reported Hypertension in 20 US States and the District of Columbia, 2019 (Am J Hypertens)
evidence.shows: About 61% of adults with hypertension reported home BP monitoring in 2019.

evidence.title: Home blood pressure monitoring and hypertension status among US adults: NHANES 2009-2010
evidence.shows: 36.6% of hypertensives monitored BP at home monthly or more.

verdicts.reading: Online patient communities that pool members' health data start to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of patients with a given condition take part in data-pooling communities by 2022 = hit; real use below 5% = partial; none by 2025 = miss.
verdicts.reason: PatientsLikeMe, the archetype, has run since 2005 with ~830,000 members, about 2% of US MS patients; it was bought by UnitedHealth in 2019 and runs on as an Optum-backed company. Real, routine use but below 5% of patients in its conditions. General online health forums (higher reach) do not pool structured health data, so are not the label's sense.

evidence.title: PatientsLikeMe (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: Over 830,000 members across 2,900 conditions; roughly 2% of US MS patients; acquired by UnitedHealth 2019.

verdicts.reading: Sensors implanted in body tissue for continuous monitoring start to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of relevant patients (e.g. CGM users, heart-failure or arrhythmia monitoring) use implanted sensors by 2022 = hit; real use below 5% = partial; none by 2025 = miss.
verdicts.reason: Fully implanted monitoring sensors are in routine but niche use: Eversense implantable CGM (FDA June 2018), CardioMEMS pulmonary-artery sensor (2014) and insertable cardiac loop recorders. Each serves a small slice of its population; most CGM users wear transcutaneous (not implanted) sensors. No evidence of 5% share by 2022.

evidence.title: FDA approves first continuous glucose monitoring system with a fully implantable glucose sensor
evidence.shows: First fully implantable CGM sensor approved (Eversense, 90 days, subcutaneous).

verdicts.reading: Powered wearable limb-assist suits like Cyberdyne's HAL start to be used in health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of relevant rehabilitation patients or facilities use HAL-type suits by 2022 = hit; real use below 5% = partial; none by 2025 = miss.
verdicts.reason: HAL received EU medical certification in 2013, Japanese medical-device approval with insurance coverage for neuromuscular diseases in 2015, and FDA clearance in 2017; it is used in a few hundred facilities. Real routine use, small share of rehab patients.

evidence.title: Hybrid Assistive Limb (Wikipedia)
evidence.shows: EC medical certificate Aug 2013; over 300 suits in 130 Japanese facilities by 2012; niche institutional rental use.

verdicts.reading: Devices that convey visual information to blind people through sound (visual-to-auditory sensory substitution) start to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of blind people or vision-rehabilitation services use it by 2022 = hit; real routine use below 5% = partial; no real use in care by 2025 = miss.
verdicts.reason: Visual-to-auditory sensory substitution (the vOICe, EyeMusic) stayed in research; reviews state only a few SSDs were ever used outside the lab and none was adopted by a wide blind community, with training as the bottleneck. No routine use in vision rehabilitation found. AI scene-description apps (Seeing AI, Be My Eyes) speak descriptions rather than substitute a sense and are not counted.

evidence.title: A self-training program for sensory substitution devices (PLoS One)
evidence.shows: Only a few visual-to-auditory/tactile SSDs used outside the lab; none adopted as main tool by a wide blind community.

evidence.title: Designing sensory-substitution devices: Principles, pitfalls and potential
evidence.shows: Auditory SSDs face adoption barriers (training, unpleasant cues).

verdicts.reading: Prosthetic limbs controlled by the user's muscle signals start to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of upper-limb amputees fitted with prostheses use myoelectric devices by 2022 = hit (earlier counts).
verdicts.reason: Myoelectric prostheses have been fitted routinely for decades; in a national study of US veterans with upper-limb amputation, 46% of recent combat veterans and 22% of Vietnam veterans used myoelectric devices. Far above 5%, already at the poster's date.

evidence.title: A national study of Veterans with major upper limb amputation: Survey methods, participants, and summary findings (PLoS One)
evidence.shows: Myoelectric device use 46% (OIF/OEF veterans) and 22% (Vietnam veterans).

verdicts.reading: Wearable powered exoskeletons that support or strengthen the body start to be used in health care (mainly rehabilitation) around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of relevant rehabilitation facilities or patients (SCI, stroke) use exoskeletons by 2022 = hit; real use below 5% = partial; none by 2025 = miss.
verdicts.reason: Medical exoskeletons (ReWalk FDA 2014, Ekso, Indego, HAL) are in routine use in rehab centres, but volumes are small: Ekso, the leading clinical vendor, booked only 100 devices in all of 2022 on $12.9M revenue. Real niche use; no evidence of 5% patient share.

evidence.title: Ekso Bionics Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2022 Financial Results
evidence.shows: 100 EksoHealth devices booked in 2022; revenue $12.9M: small clinical installed base.

verdicts.reading: Technology that extends the human sense of smell starts to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of relevant users by 2022 = hit; real routine use below 5% = partial; no real use in care by 2025 = miss.
verdicts.reason: Olfactory augmentation remains lab research: olfactory displays and an implant-style smell-restoration prosthesis (VCU) are at prototype or early human-study stage. No product in routine clinical or consumer health use by 2025. Electronic noses that diagnose disease do not extend the human sense and are not counted.

evidence.title: VCU researchers are developing a device to restore a person's sense of smell
evidence.shows: Olfactory implant/prosthesis still in development.

evidence.title: The Development of a Simple Projection-Based, Portable Olfactory Display Device
evidence.shows: Olfactory devices tested on four volunteers: research stage.

verdicts.reading: Devices interfacing with the nervous system to replace or restore function (cochlear implants, brain-controlled prostheses) start to affect health care around 2020.
verdicts.mainstream_test: D37 health: >=5% of relevant patients (e.g. severe-profound deafness) receive neuroprostheses by 2022 = hit (earlier counts).
verdicts.reason: The label explicitly includes cochlear implants: about 736,900 implanted worldwide by Dec 2019 (118,100 US adults, 65,000 US children), standard care for severe-to-profound deafness, with deep-brain stimulation also routine. Above 5% of the eligible pediatric population in high-income countries well before 2022. Brain-controlled prostheses alone would be partial (trials, Neuralink first implant 2024).

evidence.title: Cochlear Implants (NIDCD)
evidence.shows: ~736,900 cochlear implants worldwide by Dec 2019; ~183,100 in the US.
